stage: Stage 24B — first MIL experiment draft preregistration
research_question: Can customer-bag supervision over frozen temporal-window representations match or improve customer discrimination while learning reproducible instance relevance without temporal fraud labels?

data.eligible_window_rule: Existing Stage 3C usable stride-30 windows with missing_fraction < 1.0

instance_representation.name: SUMMARY_17

attention_semantics.allowed: Relative contribution or relevance of an instance to the model's customer-level representation or decision

attention_analyses.class_comparison: Report distributions for FLAG=0 and FLAG=1 as model-behaviour descriptions, not localization accuracy

perturbation.operation: Remove real instances and recompute the bag prediction; do not replace with padding or zero-valued pseudo-instances
perturbation.single_instance_bags: exclude from removal analysis and report count
perturbation.outcome: change in customer probability/logit with paired customer-level intervals

trivial_explanation_controls: Report score and attention associations with window mean, maximum, standard deviation, range, and bag size
Compare attention concentration and prediction performance within predeclared bag-size strata 1–10, 11–27, and 28–34 windows
Compare FLAG class bag-size distributions and test whether prediction is associated with bag size within each class
Use top-versus-random-versus-bottom removal to distinguish learned relevance from arbitrary removal
